definitions.explanation: Material worked into soil to enrich it, especially animal manure and compost. A more earthy, everyday word than {肥料|ひりょう}, the term used on product labels and in agriculture.

definitions.gloss: nourishment for one's growth; something that makes a person better
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, an experience — usually a painful one — that feeds later development. Used almost exclusively in the pattern 〜を{肥|こ}やしにする.

examples.japanese: {畑|はたけ}に{肥|こ}やしをやる。
examples.english: I put manure on the field.

examples.japanese: {牛|うし}のふんを{肥|こ}やしにして{野菜|やさい}を{育|そだ}てている。
examples.english: They grow vegetables using cow dung as fertilizer.

examples.japanese: この{土地|とち}は{肥|こ}やしが{足|た}りないので、{作物|さくもつ}がなかなか{育|そだ}たない。
examples.english: This land lacks fertilizer, so crops don't grow well.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}を{肥|こ}やしにする。
examples.english: To make failure into nourishment for growth.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いうちの{苦労|くろう}は、{後|のち}の{肥|こ}やしになる。
examples.english: Hardship while you're young becomes nourishment for you later on.

examples.japanese: {厳|きび}しい{批評|ひひょう}も{自分|じぶん}の{肥|こ}やしだと{考|かんが}えれば、{素直|すなお}に{聞|き}ける。
examples.english: If you think of harsh criticism as nourishment for yourself, you can take it in without resistance.

notes:
The noun of {肥|こ}やす (to fatten, to enrich). The figurative sense is far more common in conversation than the agricultural one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肥|こ}やしをやる/まく: to apply, spread manure
- {失敗|しっぱい}を{肥|こ}やしにする: to learn and grow from failure
- {経験|けいけん}が{肥|こ}やしになる: for experience to become nourishment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {肥料|ひりょう}: fertilizer — the neutral technical term, including chemical fertilizers
- {堆肥|たいひ}: compost — specifically decomposed plant and animal matter
- {糧|かて}: sustenance, food for the spirit — a more literary word for the figurative sense
